original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact full-coefficient search in F2[A4] for diag([a],[b],[aba^-1b^-1],[ab]) on four scalar registers, with the complete 240-factor alphabet D_N(g)=I+([g]+[1])N for g in {a,b}, all rank-one idempotents N in M4(F2), and the bounded question whether any word of length at most six realizes the target.
scope_change_reason: The selector suggested a target-specific relaxation bound. The session instruction requires construction-focused assignments, so the single refined scope became an exact construction search in a specified nonabelian alphabet. The group, four nontrivial outputs, paid alphabet, direct baseline, and length-six threshold are explicit; no other track or scope was substituted after acceptance.
bottleneck_link: A word of length at most six would save at least two of the eight direct paid calls in this optimistic bit-mechanism model. Excluding this target rules out that local compression mechanism before physical synthesis; no selected supplier mapping or kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Run the exact 3+3 join through all words of length at most six over all 240 factors. Stop at a verified word or after checking every left and right prefix through length three. Do not extend to length seven in this cycle.
evidence: verify.py independently reconstructs A4 and the eight-call formal matrix product, checks all 48 regular basis inputs and failure controls, then compiles and runs search.cpp. The complete join reports all 13,881,841 left prefixes, all 13,881,841 raw right prefixes, 6,697,991 distinct exact right states, a planted six-call join control, and no target word through length six.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, mathematical derivation, implementation, exact replay, and writing. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Does a seven-call word realize the four-output A4 target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A seven-call word would still reduce the direct paid bill by one call and would distinguish a six-call obstruction from a full no-sharing floor.
open_questions.first_step: Derive sharper quotient and support constraints for a 4+3 exact join, then calculate the deduplicated state and memory budget before implementing the larger search.
open_questions.blocked_by: A naive radius-four side contains more than three billion raw words; structural pruning is unproved, and the A4 alphabet has no established physical supplier mapping.
